title: String Geometric Pattern Printing & Cipher Test Paper (ICSE Class X)
prerequisites: ICSE Class X String handling methods, Scanner input, conditional branching, and loops
instructions: All questions are compulsory as per ICSE examination standards.
Write complete Java code for Section B problems including Variable Description Tables.
Pay strict attention to case sensitivity, loop bounds, and array indexing.
Each question carries marks as indicated.

sections.description: Answer in one or two sentences or evaluate the code output.

questions.answer:
Output:
```
B
BL
BLU
BLUE
BLUEJ
```
Explanation: Substring takes prefixes of increasing lengths 1 through 5.

questions.q: What arithmetic expression wraps an uppercase letter 'Z' cyclically to 'B' with a shift of 2?
questions.hint: Subtract base 'A', add shift, modulo 26, then add base 'A'.

questions.q: What character is produced by `(char)('Z' + 1)` in Java without cyclic modulo wrapping?
questions.answer:
Output: `'['` (ASCII 91)
Explanation: Java evaluates char addition as integer 90 + 1 = 91, which casts to '[' in ASCII/Unicode.

questions.q: Write the loop condition to print a word of length n in decreasing substring order: `BLUEJ`, `BLUE`, `BLU`, `BL`, `B`.
questions.hint: Count down from length down to 1.

questions.q: What is the output of `"ICSE".charAt(i)` repeated `i + 1` times for index 0 to 3?
questions.answer:
Output:
```
I
C C
S S S
E E E E
```
questions.hint: Character at index i repeated i + 1 times.

sections.description: Write complete Java programs with class declaration, main method, and Variable Description Table.

questions.q:
Write a program to input a word and display the following pattern (ICSE 2016 Pattern):
For word = "BLUEJ":
B
L L
U U U
E E E E
J J J J J
Include a Variable Description Table.
questions.hint: Outer loop runs through indices; inner loop prints charAt(i) i + 1 times.

questions.q: Write a program to accept a message in uppercase. Encrypt it using Caesar Cipher by replacing each letter with the letter 2 positions ahead (e.g. 'A' becomes 'C', 'Y' becomes 'A', 'Z' becomes 'B'). Non-alphabetic characters remain unchanged.
